subject: Annual commit cushion, burst credits, and true-up process
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Clark <jordan.clark@aerofin.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Annual commit cushion, burst credits, and true-up process

Hi Jordan,

Great talking yesterday — thanks for the context on AeroFin's planned ramp and the seasonal peaks you mentioned. Attached is a concise proposal so your procurement team can see a clear starter → growth → enterprise path. High level:

- Starter: 2M tokens / month committed (annual contract) — list price anchor $0.0010/token, offered at $0.0009/token for the first year.
- Growth: 20M tokens / month committed — tier price $0.0007/token list, proposed at $0.0006/token with a usage true-up cadence.
- Enterprise: 200M tokens / month committed — deep commitment pricing, proposed $0.00035/token with additional operational SLAs and optional Dedicated capacity.

We understand burst needs during month-end and product launches. We're proposing a "cushion": up to 30% burst above committed monthly volume available for free in year 1 (to cover launch variance), then a tiered overage rate or pre-purchased burst credits thereafter. True-up: quarterly true-up by default (can do annual true-up on request) with a one-time onboarding credit to smooth year 1.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which commit (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) you want priced into the term sheet.
2) Confirm preferred true-up cadence (quarterly/annual).
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min legal/procurement sync to walk the draft term sheet and SLA bullets.

I've attached a short PDF with the numbers and an example ramp schedule. If it helps, I can loop in our pricing lead for a quick call.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: 2026-09-15_AeroFin_Commit_Proposal.pdf (pdf - 120KB)

From: Jordan Clark <jordan.clark@aerofin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aerofin.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit cushion, burst credits, and true-up process

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear tiers. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance:

- Burst cushion: Can you clarify how the 30% is applied? Month-by-month cap, or averaged over a quarter? Any auto-throttling behavior we should know about?
- True-up cadence: Procurement prefers annual true-up for budgeting, finance prefers quarterly for forecasting accuracy. Would Redwood be open to annual true-up with quarterly reporting and a one-time true-up option if we exceed 120% of committed over the year?
- Overage billing: What SKU does Redwood use for overage charges (per-token or pre-bought burst credits)? Need an example invoice line so our AP team can map it.
- Data & contract: Please include the data handling SLA clause we discussed and any SOC2 evidence / encryption language we can share with legal.

If possible, can you add a column to the proposal that shows effective blended CPM at the projected ramp (we have an internal projection that shows a big drop after 12 months)? Also cc'ing Maya (ops) since she'll own usage monitoring.

If it's easier, let's book a short call Thursday morning PT.

Thanks —
Jordan Clark
Head of Product Ops | AeroFin
jordan.clark@aerofin.com

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit cushion, burst credits, and true-up process

Jordan / Maya —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Looping in Laura (pricing lead) and Rishi (head of enterprise sales) so we can nail the operational details. Below is an updated proposal that addresses procurement and finance asks and gives AeroFin flexibility during year 1 ramp: 

Proposed adjustments (we can bake these into the redlineable term sheet):

1) Burst cushion
   - Year 1: 30% monthly burst above committed monthly volume, applied month-by-month. No automatic throttling for bursts within the 30% cushion.
   - Year 2 onward: Burst available as pre-purchased credits (packaged SKUs) or pay-as-you-go overage at 1.5x the committed per-token rate unless a burst-pack is purchased.

2) True-up cadence
   - Default: Quarterly true-up with quarterly reporting.
   - Optional: Annual true-up with quarterly reporting and a one-time mid-year true-up option if usage exceeds 120% of the annualized committed volume. This gives finance predictability while keeping ops visibility.

3) Pricing (examples for term sheet; exact numbers will be in the attached matrix)
   - Starter (2M/mo): $0.00090 / token (year 1 intro)
   - Growth (20M/mo): $0.00060 / token (with graduated discounts at 50M and 100M annualized)
   - Enterprise (200M/mo): $0.00035 / token + optional Dedicated capacity SKU (flat monthly infrastructure fee)

4) Billing / invoice SKU guidance
   - Overage SKU: REDWOOD-OVERAGE-TOKEN (billed per-token when outside purchased burst credits)
   - Burst pack SKUs: REDWOOD-BURST-10M, REDWOOD-BURST-25M, etc.

5) Onboarding credit
   - One-time $25k onboarding credit applied to the first invoice for Enterprise and Growth closed with annual commit (helps with ramp testing and MLP releases).

6) Compliance & SLA
   - We'll provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and include the standard data-at-rest and in-transit encryption clauses in the term sheet. Rishi, can your legal ops team share a minimal data handling snippet we can include?

Attachments: I've added a compact commit matrix (AeroFin_commit_matrix.xlsx) showing blended CPM at sample ramps and a draft term-sheet link in HubSpot. Laura — note the request for blended CPM column; I included a sample projection for month 1 / month 6 / month 12.

If this looks good, I'll prepare a redlineable PDF and proposed SOW for review. Happy to do Thursday AM PT for a 25-min call to finalize.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: AeroFin_commit_matrix.xlsx (xlsx - 48KB)
